community.headline: Harlow's ECCO launches Green Lottery with first £150 draw this Friday
community.summary: The environmental charity's new fortnightly lottery will raise money for local green, community and anti-poverty projects.
body: ECCO Environmental Charity, which has worked in Harlow for more than 30 years, is launching a Green Lottery, with the first draw this Friday. Money raised will go to environmental, community and poverty-related projects in the town.

The opening draw carries a £150 cash prize, and draws will then be held every two weeks. ECCO says both the prize pot and the money for good causes can grow as more people sign up. The charity has already supported forest schools, allotments, Harlow Food Bank and cycling schemes.
The lottery is open to UK residents aged 18 and over, who can sign up through the Green Lottery website. ECCO is also promoting the scheme on Instagram.

body: Foodbanks and food charities are looking for volunteers to stand at collection points in large Tesco stores for the supermarket's Winter Food Collection, which runs from 26 to 28 November. Volunteering takes about three hours, and the charities say having people in store significantly increases how much food is given.

This is the 14th year of the collection, run with charity partners Trussell and Felix, and last year shoppers donated almost 1.5 million meals' worth of food. One in five Trussell food parcels comes from Tesco and its customers, and more than half of the charities in the Felix network, which spans over 8,000 local groups, report rising demand over the past year.

People can sign up through the Trussell or Felix websites to help at their nearest large Tesco. Trussell's co-chief executive Matthew van Duyvenbode said volunteers were urgently needed to play their part.

body: Harlow charity Rainbow Services is holding a free Ageing Well drop-in next week aimed at reducing falls among older people in the town. The event runs from 10.30am to 1pm on Wednesday 11 November at GPCA in Abercrombie Way, and everyone is welcome without booking.

Its Community Builder team has organised the morning with Princess Alexandra Hospital and other local groups, with about 25 stalls offering advice on staying safe at home and on local support. Exhibitors include Essex Police, Peabody, Essex Wellbeing Service, Hearing Help Essex, Age Well East, Essex Libraries and Action for Family Carers, alongside talks and seated exercise sessions.

Free slippers with sturdy soles and supportive backs, funded by Chas Berger, will be handed out while stocks last. Organisers point out that one in three people over 65 fall each year, and Rainbow Services can be contacted on 07701 224342.

courts.headline: Brentwood man, 50, admits stealing champagne and meat from petrol station shops

body: Scott Allaker, 50, of Beech Avenue, Brentwood, has pleaded guilty to five counts of shop theft committed between 8 August and 11 October.

Magistrates heard he took meat, wine, prosecco and champagne worth £1,117.55 in total from BP service stations including Herongate, the A13 at Orsett Cock and Hutton Mount, and from a Tesco in Brentwood. Roads policing officers stopped his car on London Road, Wickford, after a theft at the Hutton Mount site on 11 October and found eight bottles of champagne and one of prosecco.
He was given conditional bail barring him from BP, B&Q, Sainsbury's and Tesco stores in Essex and Suffolk, and is due to be sentenced on November 25.

courts.headline: Braintree driver banned after roof load smashed into armed police car on A120
courts.summary: A panel flew off his Audi near Stansted Airport, crossed the central barrier and shattered a police car's windscreen.
body: A Braintree driver whose unsecured roof load smashed into an Essex Police armed response car on the A120 near Stansted Airport has been banned from driving for a year. The panel flew off his Audi, cleared the central barrier and shattered the police car's windscreen, showering both officers with glass.

Glen Lillie, 34, of Park Drive, Braintree, pleaded guilty to three charges and was given a 12-month community order with 140 hours of unpaid work at Colchester Magistrates' Court on 22 October. The collision happened at about 1.30pm on 19 December 2025 near Little Canfield as officers drove to an emergency on blue lights. Lillie did not stop or report it, but police traced him through images of a car carrying a large flat item on a roof rack.

Police said the officer brought the damaged Volvo to a controlled stop, and the dual carriageway was closed while debris was cleared. The car was off the road for several months. PC Simon Bailey said the outcome could have been devastating and urged drivers to secure their loads.

official.headline: Great Baddow's Iron Age gold hoard goes into classrooms in new Museum of Chelmsford history kit
official.summary: Primary schools can now hire a hands-on box built around the 935 gold coins found in Great Baddow in 2020, designed with help from local pupils.
body: The Museum of Chelmsford has launched a hands-on history kit that lets primary pupils investigate one of the county's most striking finds, the Great Baddow Coin Hoard. The Baddow Discover Box is aimed at Key Stage Two classes and turns the 935 Iron Age gold coins found in Great Baddow in 2020 into a set of lessons on Chelmsford's prehistory.

The box holds 21 Iron Age activities, from handling replica artefacts to weighing up the evidence about who buried the hoard and why, and can be used as eight separate lessons or combined into an Iron Age Day. Pupils and teachers at Beehive Lane Community Primary School helped design and trial it with creative practitioner Hannelore Smith, and Westlands Community Primary and Moulsham Junior schools tested it in early 2026. It was funded by the National Lottery Heritage Fund through the Timeless Treasures project.

Schools can hire the box by the half term, with the next slot available from January 2027, and schools outside Chelmsford and Essex can borrow it too. Councillor Jennie Lardge, the city council's deputy leader, called it "all at once fun, inspiring and educational". Prices and other boxes, covering the Romans, Victorian toys and the Suffragettes, are listed on the museum's website.

The closure leaves residents in the north-west of the county without their nearest tip just as autumn garden clear-outs are under way.

According to the site's notice, the closure follows a medical incident involving a member of staff over the weekend. The centre is not expected to reopen until Monday 9 November at the earliest, and people with bookings before then will be contacted and invited to rebook.

official.headline: Basildon's Westgate car park to offer 90 minutes free from December as Aldi prepares to open
official.summary: The council has hired a new operator with number plate cameras at its Westgate Shopping Park, where Aldi's first Basildon town centre store opens on 12 November.
body: Shoppers at Basildon's Westgate Shopping Park are set to get 90 minutes of free parking from December under a new contract agreed by Basildon Borough Council. The council, which owns the shopping park, says the free period is meant to bring more people into the town centre and support its shops and leisure venues.

The council chose Sagoss Ltd to run parking at Westgate after a tender, with the decision taken on 26 October and published four days later. Number plate recognition cameras will manage the car parks and aim to cut unauthorised and long-stay parking. Basildon Today reports it is not yet clear whether the free time covers the multi-storey, the surface car park or both, or how overstays will be charged.

The scheme is expected to start in December once the contract and set-up are complete, so drivers should pay as normal until a start date is announced. Aldi's new store in Units 3 and 4 at Westgate Park opens on Thursday 12 November, and regeneration cabinet member Cllr Alex Myers said the council looked forward to welcoming it.

official.headline: Essex Police wins £30,000 to test how its drink and drug-drive crackdown deters offenders
official.summary: The Road Safety Trust is funding a 12-month study of Operation Limit, the force's drink and drug-driving enforcement campaign.
body: Essex Police is one of four forces sharing £115,000 from The Road Safety Trust for policing research. Its £30,000 grant will pay for a year-long evaluation of Operation Limit, the force's drink and drug-driving enforcement operation.

The study is meant to look beyond roadside tests, arrests and charges to how enforcement actually deters people from offending and cuts harm on the roads. Staffordshire, Hampshire and Isle of Wight, and Lincolnshire forces were also funded, taking the trust's total awards to police to nearly £700,000.
The trust's chief executive, Ruth Purdie, said policing was fundamental to road safety. A second funding round has opened, with forces able to bid for projects worth up to £30,000.

Tilbury has 25 entries, Stanford-le-Hope 18, Corringham 13 and Purfleet-on-Thames 11, while Bulphan, Horndon-on-the-Hill, Linford and Stifford Clays have one each. Thirteen entries carry a re-licensing date that has already passed, though licences may have been renewed under new entries.

A council spokesperson said HMOs tend to cluster near transport links, amenities and jobs where there is steady demand for shared housing. The figures do not show how many people live in each property.

official.headline: Medieval Southchurch Hall shuts until mid-2027 for £423,000 conservation work
official.summary: The Grade I listed moated manor house in Southend has closed to visitors while its roof, windows and stonework are repaired.
body: Southchurch Hall, the Grade I listed medieval manor house in Southend, closed to visitors on 1 November for a major conservation project. Southend-on-Sea City Council says the building is expected to stay shut until around the middle of 2027 while the work is carried out.

The £423,105 programme is funded by Arts Council England's Museums Estate and Development Fund and covers repairs to the roof and windows, conservation of the masonry, better drainage and refurbished visitor toilets. The moated hall dates from the mid-14th century and stands on the site of an earlier Saxon hall; it was a branch library from the 1930s before becoming a museum in the 1970s.

Councillor Matt Dent, cabinet member for culture, tourism and business, described the project as "once-in-a-generation conservation works" that will also improve the visitor experience. Southend Museums plans to share progress updates and behind-the-scenes stories on its social media channels while the hall is closed.

body: Harlow Rugby Club made it five straight wins with a 41-35 home victory over Wanstead at Latton Park on Saturday, Your Harlow reports. Harlow led 31-14 at the break but had to dig in after a second-half comeback from the visitors.

Brad Etherington and Dale Stalley scored early tries as Harlow raced into a 17-0 lead, and Adam Nnochiri's try plus a second for Stalley secured the bonus point. Casey Baldock added a try after the break and Liam Batty kicked five conversions and two penalties. Wanstead scored five tries, including a penalty try, and cut the gap to three points as Harlow played the last 10 minutes with 13 men after two sin-bins.
Batty's late penalty restored a six-point margin. Harlow II also extended their unbeaten run to four with a 40-17 win over East London II, and the first team travel to Woodford on 14 November.

stories.headline: Harlow Cycling Club honours Vin Denson, first Briton to win a Giro d'Italia stage
stories.summary: The club's honorary member, who rode the Tour de France alongside Jacques Anquetil and Tom Simpson, has died aged 90.
body: Harlow Cycling Club has paid tribute to Vin Denson, the pioneering professional cyclist who became one of its best-known members, after his death at the age of 90. Denson was the first British rider to win a stage of the Giro d'Italia and spent much of his later life back among Harlow's cycling community.

Denson won a Giro stage in 1966 and the Tour of Luxembourg, and rode the Tour de France as a support rider for stars including Jacques Anquetil and Rik van Loy. He was a close friend of Tom Simpson. ProCyclingUK reports he died on 14 October. He joined the Harlow clubroom in 1968 to 1969, rode for the Bantel team and in 1994 took third in the individual pursuit at the World Masters Track Championships in Manchester.

In a tribute published by Your Harlow, club member Willi Tarran remembered him as tough but kind and a constant source of encouragement for young riders, describing him as "a Giant of a man". He was made an honorary member of the club and kept turning up at its races, barbecues and social events.

body: Horse racing returned to Chelmsford City Racecourse on Monday evening for the first time since March, with Arena Racing Company (Arc) now running the track. The comeback was overshadowed by a commercial dispute, as Ladbrokes and Coral offered no betting or pictures on the eight-race card, the Racing Post reports.

Entain, which owns both bookmakers, said it is in talks with Arc and will not show Chelmsford fixtures in its shops or online until those talks conclude, leaving about 2,300 betting shops without live pictures. Arc said it looked forward to continuing positive discussions. TV coverage of the course has moved from Racing TV to Sky Sports Racing.

Racing stopped after the former licence holder, Great Leighs Estates, went into administration and the BHA blocked another company from taking over. Arc agreed a lease at the start of October and the BHA gave final approval on 23 October. The next meetings are on 5 and 26 November, followed by 3, 10 and 17 December.

body: Walsall have said they will support Colchester United goalkeeper Thimothee Lo-Tutala after a fan reportedly made a racist comment during Saturday's League Two match between the sides. A report of discriminatory language directed at a Colchester player is now being investigated by the relevant authorities.

Walsall won the game 3-1. In a joint statement, the two clubs said "discrimination of any kind will not be tolerated" and that no one, in football or wider society, should have to face it. Anyone found responsible could face arrest or a football banning order.

No details have been given of who made the report or what action has been taken so far, and the investigation is continuing. Walsall's offer of support for Lo-Tutala sits alongside the clubs' joint condemnation of the alleged abuse.

body: Colchester United suffered their first home league defeat of the League Two season on Saturday, beaten 3-1 by Walsall at the JobServe Community Stadium. The visitors were ahead inside three minutes and pulled away late on.

Declan Skura scored from close range after a corner in the third minute. Colchester thought Sean Raggett had headed an equaliser, but it was ruled out for a foul in the build-up, before Jack Payne levelled from the penalty spot in the 35th minute after Moses Sesay was fouled. Walsall keeper Jed Ward made several saves, Pressley headed the visitors back in front from Mason Hancock's cross in the 79th minute, and Clarke added a third in stoppage time.

The result ended Colchester's unbeaten home league record for the campaign. Walsall's supporters' site Bescot Banter described a much-improved second half from the visitors, who were more clinical in front of goal.

body: Southend United were beaten 3-2 by Wealdstone in the National League on Saturday after Olufela Olomola scored deep into stoppage time. It was a painful afternoon for the Shrimpers, who twice held the lead in Ruislip but left with nothing.

Leon Chambers-Parillon put Southend ahead inside five minutes when the ball broke loose in the box, but Fejiri Okenabirhie levelled from the spot on 24 minutes after Dylan Kadji was fouled. Chambers-Parillon restored the advantage with a strike from outside the area on 39 minutes. Luke Norris headed Wealdstone level just after the hour before Olomola settled it in the 94th minute.

Kieron Dyer's side went into the game third in the table on 29 points from 16 matches, with Boreham Wood top on 44. Wealdstone started the day 18th on 18 points, so the defeat was a setback for Southend's push near the top of the division.

Kieran Raynor scored in the first period before the Chieftains took control in the second period, when Rio Grinell-Parke, Lane Paddison, Callum Wells and Ollie Baldock all found the net. body: A man and a woman have been charged after three small homemade explosive devices were found at a house in Sawyers Grove, Brentwood, on Friday. The discovery led police to set up a 100-metre cordon and evacuate about 40 nearby properties while bomb disposal experts dealt with the items.

Thomas Walker, 43, is charged with three counts of criminal damage and making threats to kill, and Yolanda-Tony King, 48, with two counts of criminal damage, harassment and making threats to kill, Greatest Hits Radio reports. Both live in Sawyers Grove and were due before magistrates in Basildon on Monday 2 November. Officers had forced entry to the address at about 7.20am on Friday after reports of a disturbance.

Essex Police said inquiries into the suspicious items recovered from the address were continuing. Residents who had to leave their homes were given shelter at the King George's Playing Fields pavilion, and the cordon has since been lifted.

stories.headline: Inspectors examine Hampshire Police's handling of serious violence as Henry Nowak sentence appeals reach court tomorrow
stories.summary: A watchdog inspection of the force that first responded to the Chafford Hundred teenager's stabbing is under way, as the Court of Appeal prepares to weigh two challenges to Vickrum Digwa's 21-year minimum term on Thursday.
body: The family of Henry Nowak, the 18-year-old former Harris Academy Chafford Hundred pupil stabbed to death in Southampton in December 2025, have accused some politicians of exploiting his murder. His mother, Lucy Ross, said she was not interested in their "political game", and the family said Henry would have hated the riots that followed his death.

Henry was stabbed five times as he walked home from a night out by Vickrum Digwa, who falsely claimed Henry had racially abused him and has since been jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years. Officers handcuffed Henry as he lay dying, and his stepmother Katie Nowak said the family had been failed "multiple times". Hampshire and Isle of Wight's chief constable has apologised, saying officers failed Henry when he most needed help. The Independent Office for Police Conduct is investigating two officers for potential gross misconduct.

The Attorney General, Ellie Reeves, has referred Digwa's sentence to the Court of Appeal as unduly lenient, and Digwa himself has been given permission to challenge its length, LBC reports, with the hearing set for Thursday 5 November. LBC also reports that HM Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire and Rescue Services began inspecting Hampshire Police in October, at the request of Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones, looking at how the force handles serious violence from call-handling to first response. A separate bid by Digwa to challenge his murder conviction is still awaiting a decision, and that evening the family tell their story in the ITV Tonight special Dear Henry: Our Fight For Justice at 9pm.

body: Greater Essex is once again waiting for ministers to choose how its councils will be reorganised, after the government set out the first results of its review of the shake-up. The area now faces a choice between the three unitary councils backed by Essex County Council and the five-council model ministers chose in March, a decision that will shape who runs services such as bins, social care and planning for every resident.

Ministers originally picked five unitary councils for Essex, Southend and Thurrock in March, a model proposed by ten of the area's councils. After Reform UK took control of the county council in May it launched legal action, with leader Peter Harris calling the plan expensive and ill-thought. On 7 September the government withdrew its decisions for Essex and four other areas, citing updated legal advice, although no court had ruled them unlawful. Local Government Minister Jim McMahon announced the first review results on 29 October, East Anglia Bylines reports.

Southend-on-Sea City Council, which has consistently backed five councils, says it will keep making a robust case for that model during the review, arguing it best balances financial sustainability, local services and community identity; its leader, Councillor Daniel Cowan, said the update gives greater certainty about the timescales. Every area should know its outcome by early 2027. Elections to the existing councils go ahead in May 2027, the replacement councils would be elected in May 2028 and take over on 1 April 2029, and until then councils say services carry on as normal.

stories.summary: A signalling fault between Stanford-le-Hope and Grays hit Wednesday's morning rush, while Purfleet stays shut after the Barking freight derailment and four MPs call the disruption unacceptable.
body: c2c passengers in Thurrock faced another disrupted morning on Wednesday when a signalling failure between Stanford-le-Hope and Grays stopped trains, leaving commuters stranded at Stanford-le-Hope, East Tilbury, Tilbury and Grays, Thurrock Nub News reports. Purfleet station remains closed after the freight train derailment near Barking on 23 October, with repairs expected to run until at least the week of 9 November.

Thurrock MP Jen Craft is coordinating a joint response and has asked to meet c2c managing director Rob Mullen and Ellie Borrows, managing director of Network Rail's Eastern region. In her letter she describes the disruption as far too regular in recent months, pointing to overcrowded trains, cancellations, delays and extra travel costs, and calls c2c "an essential lifeline" for many communities. MPs Margaret Mullane, James Asser and Bayo Alaba have backed the call.

c2c said on Wednesday morning that engineers were working on the signalling fault and expected disruption until about 10am. Rail replacement buses continue between Upminster and Grays via Rainham and Purfleet while the Barking track, signalling and cabling are rebuilt, and passengers delayed may be able to claim Delay Repay.

stories.headline: Ofsted rates Essex children's services Outstanding for a third inspection in a row
stories.summary: Inspectors gave Essex County Council's support for children and families the top grade in every area, a hat-trick the council says no other authority has matched.
body: Essex County Council's children and families' services have been judged Outstanding by Ofsted, the highest grade available, after an inspection in September. The result covers support for thousands of vulnerable children, young people in care and care leavers across the county.

Inspectors gave the top grade in all four areas they now assess: the impact of leaders on social work practice, children who need help and protection, children in care, and care leavers. They praised the council's early help offer for families before problems escalate and described a skilled, stable workforce, while children in care and care leavers gave very positive feedback. The council was also rated Outstanding in 2018 and 2023 under Ofsted's previous framework.

The council says that makes Essex the only council in the country to be rated Outstanding three times in a row. Council leader Peter Harris said it was a result everyone involved should be immensely proud of, and cabinet member Sue Truman credited the dedication of staff. The full Ofsted report has been published alongside the announcement.

stories.headline: Inspectors find Castle Point's local plan unsound and press for more green belt homes
stories.summary: The planning inspectors examining the borough's blueprint say it does not provide enough housing and want extra green belt sites looked at. The council says it is extremely disappointed.
body: The government-appointed inspectors examining the Castle Point Plan have concluded that the plan, as the council submitted it, is unsound. Castle Point Borough Council published their correspondence on Tuesday evening, and the finding means the borough's long-term blueprint for where new homes go cannot be adopted in its current form, with green belt land around Benfleet, Canvey Island and Hadleigh back under the spotlight.

The letter follows the inspectors' first questions in June and a hearing in September, both of which focused on how many homes the plan proposes and whether options outside the built-up areas had been properly considered. The inspectors say more housing must be considered and want further assessment of green belt land that could take development, including extra allocations to bring the total closer to the government's standard method figure. Deputy leader Councillor Warren Gibson pointed to constraints including the green belt, wildlife sites, stretched infrastructure, congested roads and declining bus services.

Councillor Gibson said the current administration had chosen to make the most of brownfield land rather than follow the previous administration's 2022 plan, which proposed substantial green belt releases. The council says it will now seek further advice on its next steps and set out its position once that work is done, though it has given no date. Strategic planning portfolio holder Councillor Tim Copsey said the focus remained on doing what is right for the borough.

stories.headline: Essex council leader calls SEND officers 'world class' after cabinet member quits over care plan refusals
stories.summary: Reform UK leader Peter Harris has backed County Hall's special needs staff, calling Sam Journet's criticism a normal political difference of opinion, as Halstead councillor Isi Rocha takes on the brief.
body: Essex County Council's cabinet member for education, special educational needs and skills has resigned after criticising how officers have dealt with applications for education, health and care plans (EHCPs). Cllr Sam Journet, the Reform UK member for Vange, said some of what he had seen from officers had shocked him, in a dispute that goes to the heart of support for thousands of Essex families.

In a letter to council leader Cllr Peter Harris, Mr Journet said he had directed officers to reconsider some refused EHCP requests but this had not happened, adding he wanted decisions reviewed rather than any particular outcome. A council report recently said only 17% of plans in Essex were issued within the 20-week legal limit, and requests have risen by 1,900 to 4,706 compared with five years ago. Mr Journet said he was stepping down to focus on his role at Basildon Council.

Essex County Council leader Cllr Peter Harris has now defended the officers, describing them as highly professional and saying he is fully supportive of them, while praising Mr Journet's work. He promised what he called the biggest investment in SEND education the county has seen, though no details were given. Cllr Isi Rocha, who represents Halstead, was chosen on Monday to take over the portfolio, and Mr Journet remains a backbench councillor.

body: A 60-year-old Grays man accused of brandishing what turned out to be a toy gun in the town centre has denied a firearms charge and been sent for trial at crown court, Thurrock Nub News reports. Armed police were called to Grays on Monday 2 November after numerous reports of a man with a firearm, and he was arrested and held overnight.

Martin Heward, of Palmers Avenue, Grays, appeared before Basildon magistrates on Tuesday charged with possessing an imitation firearm with intent to cause fear of violence and with racially aggravated harassment of a woman. He pleaded not guilty to the firearm charge and was released on conditional bail, including an electronic tag, a curfew at his home and a ban on contacting the woman involved.

He is due at Basildon Crown Court on Friday 4 December on the firearm charge, and will return to Basildon Magistrates' Court at a later date to enter a plea on the second charge. He has not been convicted of any offence.

body: A man has been charged after a pedestrian was left with life-changing injuries in a collision in Waltham Abbey town centre. Arren Lewis, 36, is accused of causing grievous bodily harm with intent, failing to stop and dangerous driving, Essex Police said.

The charges relate to an incident at about 5pm on 8 October in North Place, when a man in his 30s was reportedly struck by a grey Audi TT. He suffered significant injuries to his legs and was taken to hospital, while the driver is alleged to have left the scene.

Lewis is due to appear at Snaresbrook Crown Court on 19 November. Detectives are still appealing for anyone with doorbell or dashcam footage or other information to come forward, with Detective Constable James Refalo saying "no detail is too small".

Leicestershire's penalty was imposed for a breach of the ECB's pitch regulations, and the disciplinary panel's decision has now been upheld. Essex thanked its members, supporters and sponsors for their loyal backing during what it called a period of uncertainty, and pointed fans to the Cricket Regulator's website for full details of the ruling.

Off the field, the club has also put back its membership price rise. Members from 2026 who have not yet renewed can still do so at the members' price until 11.59pm on Monday 9 November, with prices going up on Tuesday 10 November.

stories.headline: MPs' standards watchdog finds South Basildon MP James McMurdock started racial slur chain but takes no action
stories.summary: A Commons committee rejected the independent MP's explanations for a one-letter post on X but ruled the damage was to his own reputation, not Parliament's.
body: James McMurdock, the independent MP for South Basildon and East Thurrock, will face no further action after a Commons standards investigation into a social media post, Thurrock Nub News reports. The Standards Committee's report, published on Tuesday, found he posted the letter "N" on X in August 2025 beneath a post criticising Sky News political reporter Mhari Aurora, starting a chain of posts that spelled out a racial slur against her.

The committee rejected his claims that a child had posted the letter or that it was posted by accident, and found on the balance of probabilities that he posted it himself. Standards commissioner Daniel Greenberg concluded he had breached the MPs' code of conduct and had taken no steps to distance himself from the slur. But the committee ruled he had not broken the rule on causing significant damage to the reputation of the House, saying any harm was to his own reputation, and recommended no further action.

Mr McMurdock, who was elected for Reform UK in 2024 before leaving the party, called the investigation a "ridiculous waste of taxpayers' money" and said he was glad a rational conclusion had been reached. He said he was mortified when he saw what followed his post and looked forward to moving on.
points: Standards Committee report published on 3 November
Committee found he posted the letter himself
No breach of the rule on damaging the reputation of the House
No further action recommended

stories.headline: First sketch of Better Queensway's next phase shows homes plan for Southend city centre car park sites
stories.summary: Southend council has given a first look at the opening development zones of its regeneration scheme as it seeks a commercial partner to help pay for future phases.
body: Southend-on-Sea City Council has published an illustrated sketch giving the first view of the next stage of its Better Queensway regeneration in the city centre. The drawing covers the first two development zones, where the council has previously proposed up to 1,000 homes in the early phases.

The zones take in The Range and Short Street car park site, Quantock Tower and the former Essex Street car park site, and the image has been posted on the council's Flickr channel. Council leader Daniel Cowan called the scheme a "once-in-a-generation opportunity" for the heart of the city.

Subject to Cabinet approval, the council plans to set up an Investment Partnership with a commercial organisation so that later phases can be funded and delivered. A joint scrutiny meeting of the Policy and Resources Overview and Scrutiny Committee will examine the plans on Thursday 12 November at 6.30pm.
points: Sketch covers the first two development zones
Sites include Quantock Tower and two former car parks
Up to 1,000 homes previously proposed in first phases
Scrutiny meeting on 12 November at 6.30pm

stories.headline: Shania Twain and FIVE named as first 2027 festival headliners for Chelmsford
stories.summary: The country star tops the bill at State Fayre in June, while the 90s pop group will open the second Chelmsford Summer Series in August.
body: Chelmsford has secured two big names for its 2027 summer of music, with Shania Twain announced as the first headliner for the American-themed State Fayre festival and FIVE confirmed as the first act for the second Chelmsford Summer Series. Both announcements came this week and point to the city's growing pull for major outdoor shows.

Twain, 61, will play State Fayre on Saturday 19 June, the middle day of the 18 to 20 June festival, according to the Press Association. The 2026 event at Hylands Park drew more than 50,000 people, and the first wave of weekend and Saturday tickets goes on sale at 9am on Friday 6 November through the festival's website. FIVE will play Central Park on Friday 27 August, 30 years after the band formed, the BBC reported.

Organisers of both events say more acts will follow. Louder Entertainment runs the Summer Series, which featured McFly, Sugababes and Craig David this year, and Chelmsford City Council deputy leader Jennie Lardge said the festival reflects the city's ambitions as a destination for culture and events.
points: Shania Twain plays State Fayre on 19 June 2027
State Fayre tickets on sale 9am Friday 6 November
FIVE headline Central Park on 27 August 2027
More acts for both festivals still to come

stories.headline: Chadwell St Mary campaigners rally objections to 385-home plan on farmland north of the village
stories.summary: Opponents want residents to write to Thurrock Council before the comment window on the application closes later this month.
body: Campaigners in Chadwell St Mary are urging residents to have their say on a planning application for up to 385 homes on arable land to the north of the village. The scheme was submitted to Thurrock Council in May and is the latest in a series of development proposals around Chadwell, Thurrock Nub News reports.

Opponents are asking people to explain in their own words why the plan worries them, pointing to the loss of farmland and green space, the impact on wildlife, extra traffic and added pressure on roads, schools and other local services. Comments can be made through the council's online planning portal.

The council will weigh the application alongside the public comments, and campaigners hope a strong response will persuade councillors to turn it down. No decision date has been given, and the comment period is due to close later in November.
points: Up to 385 homes proposed on farmland north of Chadwell St Mary
Application lodged with Thurrock Council in May 2026

stories.headline: Remembrance poppies painted on roads in 12 Essex towns, from Dunmow to Clacton
stories.summary: Essex County Council is marking Remembrance with poppy emblems on the road surface in a dozen places, and says it is also spending on the upkeep of war memorials.
body: Essex County Council is painting Remembrance poppies on roads in 12 towns across the county as a tribute to those who died in service and those who served. The emblems will be seen by drivers, cyclists and pedestrians in the run-up to Remembrance Sunday.

The locations are Dunmow High Street, Harlow, Brentwood, Hadleigh, Pitsea, Epping, Braintree, Rochford, Chelmsford, Maldon, Clacton and Colchester. Council leader Peter Harris said the poppies would be a "powerful visual tribute", while highways cabinet member Mark Webster, himself a veteran, said it mattered to keep honouring those who died serving the country.

The council says it is also investing in refurbishing and maintaining war memorials so they stay fitting places for reflection. Its armed forces champion, Terry Longstaff, said the emblems showed the county's commitment to preserving the legacy of those who served.
points: 12 locations across the county
Tribute to the fallen and those who served
War memorials also being refurbished
Announced by Essex County Council

stories.headline: Grays river spill features as BBC maps where Anglian Water pollution is worst
stories.summary: Campaigners want faster investment in sewers across the region, while Anglian Water says its bathing waters are the cleanest since current rules began in 2015.
body: A BBC look at pollution across the Anglian Water region has highlighted the River Mardyke at Grays, where about 3,500 tonnes of untreated sewage entered the river last year and thousands of fish died. Campaigners say spending on sewers and pumping stations is too slow to protect rivers and the coast that Essex families use.

Anglian Water says storm overflow spills fell by 62% in 2025 compared with 2024 and pollution events by 16%, with 340 storm overflows permanently taken out of use. It says 96.3% of its designated bathing waters are rated good or excellent, the highest share in England, but Surfers Against Sewage counted 501 sewage alerts at its bathing waters in 2025, a figure the company accepted was broadly correct.

The company says it plans to spend more than £2bn on environmental improvements and accepts it has more to do. Environment Secretary Dame Angela Eagle has said she is demanding answers from failing water firms, after regulators rated eight of England's nine water companies poor or requiring improvement.
points: About 3,500 tonnes of untreated sewage reached the River Mardyke at Grays last year
Storm overflow spills down 62% in 2025, Anglian Water says
501 sewage alerts at Anglian bathing waters in 2025

stories.headline: Former Essex PC who assaulted a paramedic in Chelmsford would have been sacked, panel rules
stories.summary: A misconduct hearing found ex-PC Rebecca Brennan committed gross misconduct after she admitted attacking a paramedic while off duty.
body: A former Essex Police officer who assaulted a paramedic while off duty would have been dismissed without notice had she not already resigned, a misconduct panel has found. The case involved an ambulance call to an address in Chelmsford in February.

Former PC Rebecca Brennan admitted the assault and was fined £500 and ordered to pay £500 compensation at Ipswich Magistrates' Court on 4 August. An accelerated misconduct hearing at Essex Police headquarters on Friday 30 October found she had breached professional standards on discreditable conduct.
Chief Constable Rachel Nolan said violence in any form was not acceptable, and that the force would not tolerate officers, staff or volunteers who thought such behaviour was acceptable.
points: Off-duty assault on a paramedic in Chelmsford in February
£500 fine and £500 compensation at Ipswich magistrates

stories.headline: Scaled-back plan for four more Traveller pitches in Fobbing goes to Thurrock Council
stories.summary: The applicants have cut a rejected nine-pitch scheme on Mill Lane to four, arguing Thurrock is short of Traveller sites.
body: A fresh planning application seeks to expand a Traveller site on Mill Lane in Fobbing from one authorised pitch to five, months after Thurrock Council turned down a bigger scheme. The council refused a plan for nine extra pitches in July, citing harm to the openness of the green belt and the rural character of the area.

The new proposal would add four pitches, each with one static mobile home and one touring caravan, and existing stables and containers would be removed. Two of the pitches are intended for the applicants' children when they reach adulthood, and two would help meet unmet need for Traveller accommodation in the borough. An ecological assessment has been submitted alongside a proposed 10 per cent biodiversity net gain.

The planning statement argues that only seven pitches were approved and built in Thurrock between 2016 and 2021, against earlier evidence of need for at least 78, and that the council cannot show a five-year supply of sites. Thurrock Council will now decide whether to grant permission.

stories.headline: National law firm Geldards opens first East of England office in Chelmsford
stories.summary: The firm, which already has offices in Cardiff, Derby, Nottingham and London, says more hires will follow in the coming weeks.
body: Law firm Geldards has opened an office in Chelmsford, its first in the East of England, saying the move responds to local demand from businesses and public bodies. The expansion brings another professional services employer to the city centre's growing business community.

The office is led by partner Thomas Emmett, who heads the firm's schools, colleges and universities practice and advises on academy mergers, independent school deals and nursery group sales. He is joined by commercial property lawyer Jennifer Rayner, employment solicitor Charlotte Holman and corporate paralegal Sarah Hawkins. Chief executive Jeff Pearson called the opening a significant milestone in the firm's expansion strategy.

Geldards says further appointments to the Chelmsford team will be made in the coming weeks. The move was reported in the legal and business trade press, including Local Government Lawyer and Insider Media.
points: First Geldards office in the East of England

stories.headline: Essex Libraries marks 100 years with exhibitions, reading challenges and a call for memories
stories.summary: The county library service, founded in 1926, is running centenary events at branches across Essex this autumn.
body: Essex Libraries is celebrating its 100th birthday, with events, exhibitions and activities running in branches across the county through the autumn. The service was set up in 1926 and Essex County Council is encouraging residents to drop in to their local library to mark the centenary.

The programme includes special exhibitions, reading challenges and children's activities, and residents are being invited to share their own memories of using their library. The council points out that libraries now offer far more than books, including digital services, learning, local history resources and community events. Councillor Chris Hossack, cabinet member for residents and community services, said libraries had been at the heart of Essex communities for a century, and council chairman Councillor Karen McIvor has been visiting branches in recent weeks.

Details of upcoming centenary events are being posted on the Essex Libraries website and its social media channels. The celebrations continue through the autumn, alongside the libraries' regular programme of activities.
points: Essex Libraries was founded in 1926
Centenary exhibitions and activities at branches this autumn
Residents invited to share library memories
Reading challenges and children's events planned

stories.headline: Harlow man, 53, charged with three assaults on a woman and damaging a phone
stories.summary: Police say the alleged assaults took place in Harlow over the summer and in October; he has been released on conditional bail.
body: A 53-year-old Harlow man has been charged with three counts of assault by beating against a woman and one count of criminal damage, Your Harlow reports. Kevin Hanson, of Woodbine Close, Harlow, has not been convicted of any offence.

The assault charges relate to dates in July 2026, on 29 August and on 20 October, all in Harlow. The criminal damage charge alleges that on 20 October he damaged an iPhone worth £300 belonging to another person.
He has been released on conditional bail and the case is listed at Chelmsford Magistrates' Court.

Criminal damage to a £300 phone alleged

stories.headline: Bicknacre powerlifter, 64, wins Commonwealth gold months after tiny pacemaker fitted
stories.summary: Specialists at the Essex Cardiothoracic Centre chose a wire-free device so a lifting bar would not rest on it.
body: Nicky Solis, a 64-year-old powerlifter from Bicknacre, has won gold at the Commonwealth Championships in Canada only months after needing a pacemaker. She fell unexpectedly ill in the summer and doctors found her heart rate was very low.

A standard pacemaker sits under the skin near the collarbone, where a powerlifting bar rests, so specialists at the Essex Cardiothoracic Centre, run by Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust, fitted a leadless device instead. The procedure was carried out by consultant cardiologist Dr Christine Menexi. Leadless pacemakers have no wires, sit inside the heart and are about 90 per cent smaller than traditional models.
The championships took place in September, and the trust has shared her story to highlight the treatment. The report did not give her lifts or weight class.
points: Nicky Solis is 64 and from Bicknacre
Gold at the Commonwealth Championships in Canada
Leadless pacemaker fitted at the Essex Cardiothoracic Centre
Device sits inside the heart, with no wires

stories.headline: Moulsham Street traders call for return of Chelmsford Christmas parade axed in 2012
stories.summary: Shopkeepers say bringing back the festive procession would help a street they feel has never fully recovered from lockdown.
body: Traders on Chelmsford's Moulsham Street want the return of the Christmas parade that once filled the street with performers, festive lights and sweets thrown to children. The event ended in 2012, and shopkeepers believe reviving it could help draw shoppers back to one of the city's oldest trading streets.

Elena Marinina of G Dawson and Sons jewellers remembered every shop decorated and Santa visiting, and said a parade would help bring trade back. Terry Woodham of Large Men's clothing said the street had not bounced back since lockdown and that people now come into Chelmsford mainly to eat and drink. Garry Debrick of Franklins sewing machine shop backed a return but was more upbeat, estimating that Moulsham Street and the city centre are about 90 per cent occupied.

Chelmsford City Council said it had not been approached about a new event on the street but would be happy to discuss ideas and support traders. It noted that past events were led by the Moulsham Street Traders' Association, while the city's Business Improvement District, set up in 2018, runs the main lights switch-on and the Christmas in the City programme. All of Chelmsford's Christmas lights, including those on Moulsham Street, are being updated this year.

Council says it would support traders who come forward
All city Christmas lights being updated this year

features.headline: Essex kitchens clean up at the 2026 'Curry Oscars'
features.summary: A Colchester restaurant took both the county and national chef titles, and Kelvedon Spice was named Essex Restaurant of the Year.
body: Essex restaurants and takeaways had a strong night at the 2026 Asian Restaurant and Takeaway Awards, the ceremony often called the Curry Oscars. Essex Life reports that county venues won regional titles and two of the night's national prizes.

Kusturi Indian Restaurant in Colchester was named both Essex Chef of the Year and National Chef of the Year, while Kelvedon Spice won Essex Restaurant of the Year. Kaani Kaana in Upminster took Essex Takeaway of the Year and the national takeaway title. Moonlight Tandoori in Harlow, Crown of India in Loughton and Pink Chilliz on Canvey were among the other Essex finalists.

The awards were presented on October 12 at the London Hilton on Park Lane, hosted by news presenter Samantha Simmonds and comedian Paul Sinha. ARTA founder and chief executive Mohammed Munim congratulated all the winners and finalists.

features.headline: From hedgerow to cheeseboard: what to eat in Essex this autumn
features.summary: Essex Life asks a forager and an award-winning cheesemaker what the county's larder has to offer as the nights draw in.
body: Apples, oysters, game, honey and cheese all hit their stride in autumn, and Essex Life has gone looking for the best of the county's seasonal larder, with a few foraged surprises along the way.

At The Foraging Chef, the season is treated as an adventure: wild mushrooms, and hedgerow fruits such as rosehips, crab apples and sloes, are at their peak. Muntjac also feature, with the case made that eating the deer puts a plentiful local food to use while helping to keep numbers in check.

Bradfields Farm Dairy talks through the cheeses locals keep coming back for, including its soft Beam and an Essex herb cheese. For a warm autumn day it suggests its Bourne Brook spread over a barbecue skewer with aubergines and marmande tomatoes from Sarah Green Organics and a drizzle of Essex rapeseed oil.
points: Foraged mushrooms and hedgerow fruits at their best
Muntjac on the menu at The Foraging Chef
Bradfields Farm Dairy's autumn cheese picks

features.headline: Autumn staycations close to home, from Mersea huts to woodland lodges
features.summary: Glamping on Mersea Island, coastal cottages, vineyard stays, spa breaks and woodland lodges all make Essex Life's autumn escape list.
body: Essex Life has rounded up places to stay in the county this autumn for every taste and age, from glamping and coastal cottages to vineyard retreats, spa breaks and woodland lodges.

Mersea Barns Glamping in East Mersea has four luxury units on five acres of rural Mersea Island. Managing director Anthea Sanderson explains that its shepherd huts open all year and sleep two, with full-size double beds, built-in kitchens and shower rooms.
Elsewhere on the list, another featured stay has revamped two of its most secluded lodges for 2026 as couples-only retreats.
points: Four glamping units on five acres at East Mersea
Shepherd huts open all year, sleeping two
Vineyard, spa and woodland options also featured

features.headline: An eight-mile ramble along the Mardyke, one of Essex's least-known rivers
features.summary: A countryside circuit from South Ockendon's round-tower church follows the Mardyke Way past fields, solar farms and wildlife.
body: Essex Life's latest walk starts at St Nicholas of Myra Church on The Green in South Ockendon and loops for about eight miles along the Mardyke Way. The Mardyke, sometimes written Mar Dyke, is a small, overgrown river in a wide, flat valley crossed by the M25 and A13 near junction 30.

South Ockendon has been a village since at least Saxon times, with signs of Roman settlement near South Ockendon Hall. Its church keeps fine Norman details and is one of only six in Essex with a round tower. The route heads out past the Royal Oak pub and the hall before crossing the river by a metal footbridge.
Ockendon station is about 500 metres from the start along West Road. Davy Down Riverside Park, just west of the route, has parking and toilets.

Ockendon station 500m from the start

features.headline: A £1.5m Wickham Bishops home with its own garden bar
features.summary: This six-bedroom detached house is built for entertaining, with an outdoor kitchen, a piano room and two floors of bedrooms.
body: Essex Life's property pick this week is a six-bedroom detached home in the village of Wickham Bishops, on the market at £1.5 million.

The ground floor has a living room, sitting room, separate dining room, a study and a piano room, built around a large kitchen and diner that opens on to the garden. Four bedrooms are on the first floor, many with en suites and walk-in wardrobes, and two more sit on the second floor with a family bathroom.
Outside, extensive private gardens include a garden bar and outdoor kitchen, with a double garage and further outbuildings for storage.
points: Six bedrooms over three floors
Garden bar and outdoor kitchen
Guide price £1.5m

features.headline: Step inside a painting: Simon Carter turns Firstsite into an Essex shoreline
features.summary: The Frinton artist's biggest show yet fills Colchester's gallery with painted walls, sea-defence 'groynes' and sounds recorded on the coast.
body: Frinton-based painter Simon Carter has turned Firstsite in Colchester into a walk-through painting for From the Landscape, the largest exhibition of his career.

The show blends painting, architecture and sound. Carter has built monolithic walls modelled on the groynes that protect the Essex shoreline, and added a soundscape made from his own recordings of the coast. Firstsite director Sally Shaw says he has been quietly mapping the Essex landscape for more than forty years.
The exhibition is supported by the Firstsite Collectors' Group and Trevor Fenwick, and is listed to run until 17 January 2027.
points: Carter's largest exhibition to date
Gallery walls echo coastal groynes
